atlas-cz.0130: ABSL’s 2025 report says English is the common language of business in the service centres, which use many languages; EURES says nearly all other employers require Czech.
atlas-cz.0131: Komerční banka’s trainee and careers pages are in Czech and state no English or other language requirement.
atlas-cz.0132: Red Hat’s Brno internship asks for working knowledge of written and spoken English, and JetBrains’ internship page states no language requirement; Czech is not mentioned in either.
atlas-cz.0133: The civil-service selection procedures are published in Czech on ISoSS; we did not read a stated language level.
atlas-cz.0134: Eurostat’s figures show 86.1% of recent tertiary graduates aged 20–34 in work in 2025 (EU 85.3%) and youth unemployment of 10.4%. We found no return-offer or conversion rate for the Czech Republic.
atlas-cz.0135: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens work with no authorisation; the employer notifies the labour office by the first day.
atlas-cz.0136: Staying over 30 days in a private flat, report your address to the foreigners’ police within 30 days; hotels and registered dorms do it for you.
atlas-cz.0137: The registration certificate after three months is optional (CZK 200), but in practice banks and landlords ask for it.
atlas-cz.0138: Long-term visa and residence for study
atlas-cz.0139: Full-time students on accredited university programmes may work without a work permit or hours limit; private language courses give no right to work.
atlas-cz.0140: Funds must be in an account in your own name, with an international card linked to it; health insurance must be a comprehensive policy of at least €400,000 with no excess.
atlas-cz.0141: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country in an EU programme can stay up to 360 days without a Czech visa, after the university notifies the immigration department (OAMP).
atlas-cz.0142: CZK 115,810 for a year, CZK 78,250 for a semester
atlas-cz.0145: For students abroad or graduates of the last two years, with a written traineeship agreement covering the training plan, supervision, pay or allowance, housing and health cover.
atlas-cz.0146: An internship within a Czech degree needs no work permit.
atlas-cz.0147: Stay to look for work or start a business
atlas-cz.0148: After a Czech degree, apply in person before your study permit expires: nine months, not renewable. You may also open a business straight away.
atlas-cz.0149: Anyone who completes an accredited Czech degree has free access to the labour market for life: a job only needs the non-dual employee card.
atlas-cz.0151: Since July 2024 there is no waiting period on the job advert: you apply as soon as the vacancy is in the labour office register. UK and US citizens (and seven other countries) have free access to work and get the simpler non-dual card.
atlas-cz.0152: At least 15 hours a week at the minimum wage; you cannot change employer in the first six months, and later only after notifying the ministry 30 days ahead.
atlas-cz.0155: CZK 5,000 abroad, CZK 2,500 in the country
atlas-cz.0156: A first employee card cannot be applied for in the country after a visa-free entry: file it at a consulate abroad.
atlas-cz.0157: A contract of at least six months for highly qualified work and a three-year degree, or for IT three years of experience in the last seven; the card lasts up to three years, and family can join at once.
atlas-cz.0160: A hosting agreement with a research organisation on the approved register; free access to work for the project, family reunion at once, and nine months after the project to find a job.
atlas-cz.0161: A doctoral stipend is free of income tax and social contributions.
atlas-cz.0162: The Czech Republic has working-holiday agreements only with New Zealand, Canada, South Korea, Israel, Chile, Japan, Australia, Taiwan and Peru.
atlas-cz.0163: For citizens of the partner countries aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canada): 12 months, not convertible to any other permit inside the country.
atlas-cz.0165: Up to 90 days in any 180, with no work beyond a few short exempt activities. Staying privately, non-EU visitors report to the foreigners’ police within three working days.
atlas-cz.0166: Nothing to arrange in advance: you need no visa or work permit, and your employer notifies the labour office by your first day of work.
atlas-cz.0167: Apply for your first permit at a Czech consulate abroad: even visa-free nationals (UK, US) cannot switch from a short stay to a work permit inside the country.
atlas-cz.0168: Check the flat is registered as a dwelling, and that a sublet has the owner’s written consent: otherwise it is not valid proof of housing. Have translations done by a translator sworn in the Czech Republic.
atlas-cz.0169: Staying more than 30 days in private housing, report your address to the Foreign Police within 30 days of arriving; hotels and registered student residences do it for you. Missing it can be fined up to 3,000 CZK.
atlas-cz.0170: In a private flat or short-term rental, report to the Foreign Police in person within 3 working days of arriving, or face a fine of up to 3,000 CZK.
atlas-cz.0171: The registration certificate (osvědčení o registraci) for stays over 3 months is optional and costs 200 CZK, but banks, car registration and parking permits ask for it.
atlas-cz.0172: Collect your residence card from the Interior Ministry’s office (OAMP). The legal processing time is 60 to 90 days; in practice it takes 3 to 6 months.
atlas-cz.0173: The registration certificate is in practice what gets you a Czech personal number (rodné číslo) without delay.
atlas-cz.0174: Employees are enrolled in public health insurance through their employer, with a fund such as VZP.
atlas-cz.0175: EU students use their European Health Insurance Card.
atlas-cz.0176: Students and others not employed need comprehensive private insurance covering at least €400,000 with no deductible, typically 10,000 to 14,000 CZK a year; a policy with a deductible is refused.
atlas-cz.0177: Banks ask for the registration certificate before a mortgage.
atlas-cz.0178: Students prove funds with a statement from an account in their own name only, with a copy of the card linked to it.
atlas-cz.0179: Renew between 120 days before and the last day of your permit: one day late and the status is lost.
atlas-cz.0180: The paper receipt is valid only inside the Czech Republic; before travelling, have the free bridging sticker (překlenovací štítek) put in your passport at OAMP.
atlas-cz.0181: Attend the 4-hour integration course within 1 year of collecting your permit (1,500 CZK), or face a fine of up to 10,000 CZK; and tell OAMP within 3 working days if your job ends.
atlas-cz.0182: Renew between 120 days before and the last day of your permit: one day late and you lose your status and the years towards permanent residence.
atlas-cz.0183: The paper receipt is valid only inside the Czech Republic: before any trip while you wait, get the free bridging visa sticker at OAMP.
atlas-cz.0184: A sublet needs the registered owner’s written consent, and a non-residential unit (atelier) cannot be your address.
atlas-cz.0185: Attend the four-hour integration course within a year of getting an employee card, or face fines up to CZK 10,000.
atlas-cz.0186: Report the end of a job to OAMP within three working days, or the card can be withdrawn.
atlas-cz.0187: Non-EU residents of Italy and other Schengen countries apply through the consulate in Dresden, which requires two years of legal residence in Schengen.
atlas-cz.0188: Employee cards take 4 to 8 months in Prague and Brno, against a legal 60 to 90 days.
atlas-cz.0189: A new immigration code, fully digital, is before parliament.
